quoted_clause: A startup's CTO shows the architect a warrant to buy two 8×H100 servers for the new internal RAG assistant

'8×H100' is also ambiguous between per-host and per-replica (the canonical fleet's 21 hosts at 70B FP16 imply either 21 or 84 replicas depending on topology).
correction: Add one sentence giving the assumed model and topology (e.g., 'same 70B FP16, 2 GPUs per replica → 8 replicas across the two hosts; 2 rps average is 0.25 rps/replica, well inside the 0.48 rps/replica the canonical fleet sustains at its 40 rps peak'), and state the per-replica load explicitly.
evidence: Canonical: 21 hosts × 8 GPUs = 168 GPUs; 70B FP16 = 140 GB → 2 GPUs/replica → 84 replicas at 40 rps peak (0.48 rps/replica). Mini-case: 2 hosts = 16 GPUs → 8 replicas at 2 rps average (0.25 rps/replica) — comfortably inside the canonical's demonstrated per-replica capability, but only if the topology is stated.

quoted_clause: flat because the fleet is paid regardless of volume
observed: The self-host cost formula includes energy, which is not strictly volume-invariant. The text describes the line as flat without stating that energy is modeled as fixed or idle-dominated. A reader could infer that self-host cost is exactly constant across all served volumes, which is false if energy scales with utilization.

evidence: The formula is '(capex ÷ 60 mo) + energy + staff/ops'. Energy is a function of load, cooling, and utilization. Only capex amortization and staff/ops are plausibly fixed. The figure's flat-line claim therefore depends on an unstated fixed-energy assumption.

quoted_clause: FP8 changes only the KV arithmetic
observed: The sentence is too broad. FP8 can refer to FP8 weights, FP8 activations, FP8 KV cache, or FP8 compute. In this paragraph the intended meaning is FP8 KV quantization, which changes the KV byte factor. But as written, 'FP8 changes only the KV arithmetic' implies FP8 has no effect on weights, compute throughput, memory residency, or kernels, which is false in general.
correction: Change to: 'FP8 KV quantization changes only the KV arithmetic in this screen: the raw FP8 byte factor 0.5 gives a hard floor of 35 slots...' Add a sentence: 'FP8 weights or FP8 compute would change other screens and are not modeled here.'
evidence: The surrounding calculation uses only the FP8 KV byte factor 0.5 to halve the per-token KV footprint. It does not model FP8 weights or FP8 compute. The sentence should be scoped to that screen.

quoted_clause: H_\text{cloud,month} = \text{paid host-hours (an occupancy INPUT, supplied or assumed)}
observed: The same symbol H_cloud,month is defined twice: first as an occupancy input supplied or assumed, then immediately as the integral of required capacity over time plus warm-pool and reservation terms. These are different quantities. The first is a billing input; the second is a derived load-duration integral. Using one symbol for both makes the cloud-cost model ambiguous and undermines the later distinction between paid host-hours and required capacity.
correction: Use distinct symbols, e.g. H_paid for the billing input and H_required for the load-duration integral. State explicitly that the default 4,380 host-hours is an assumed H_paid, not an evaluation of H_required. Then the cloud-cost equation can be written as Cost = p_host × H_paid, with H_paid ≥ H_required plus warm-pool and reservation terms.
evidence: The first equation defines H_cloud,month as an input. The second equation defines H_cloud,month = ∫ N_required(t) dt plus warm/startup pool and capacity reservation. The text then says the default bills 6 × 730 host-hours, which is neither the integral nor a proven feasible schedule.

page_hint: Chapter 16, fleet-sizing table, case (ii) prefill row and the later 34-host derivation

quoted_clause: more volume only widens the ~$64K gap
observed: The claim ignores the two servers' capacity limit. At some volume the two-server deployment cannot serve the load, so self-host cost would step up with additional servers. 'More volume only widens the gap' is true only within the two-server capacity headroom.
correction: Qualify the sentence: 'within the two-server capacity headroom, more volume widens the gap; beyond that, additional servers step the self-host cost up.' State the assumed peak rps or capacity bound.
evidence: The mini-case gives ~2 rps average and ~5M requests/month but does not state the peak capacity or headroom of two 8×H100 servers for this workload. Without that bound, the monotonic claim is unsupported.

quoted_clause: re-price on one staffing basis before comparing
observed: The mini-case explicitly says the startup's 0.5-FTE staffing basis (~$26K/mo for two hosts) differs from Mode 1's mature-operator allocation (~$10K/mo for 21 hosts), and says to re-price before comparing. It then proceeds to compare the $40K self-host cost (which includes the $26K/mo startup wage) against the API and reaches a verdict without re-pricing or showing sensitivity.
correction: Either re-price both options on one staffing basis, or label the verdict explicitly as conditional on the startup's $26K/mo scenario and add a sensitivity row for Mode 1's $10K/mo allocation. The conclusion should not read as general.
evidence: If the two-host deployment were priced on Mode 1's ~$10K/mo staff allocation, self-host cost would fall to roughly $11.6K + $2.2K + $10K = $23.8K/mo, changing the cash gap from $64K to ~$80.2K/mo. The verdict 'start on the managed API now' is therefore conditional on the startup-specific staffing basis, but the text presents it as the architect's verdict.

quoted_clause: revisit self-host the moment the consumed engineer's opportunity cost falls below ~$64K/month — for example when a second engineer frees up
observed: The second-engineer branch is stated without the condition that makes it work. Hiring a second engineer adds cash cost that is not in the $40K; the branch is valid only if that engineer was already on the plan (or if the displaced product work is worth less than their cost). As written, 'a second engineer frees up' is offered as a free lever, and the closing sentence 'runs the same numbers and buys the servers' contradicts the earlier 're-run the same model'.
correction: Qualify the branch: 'if a second engineer is already on the hiring plan, self-hosting becomes strictly better (the freed 0.5 FTE returns to product work while the $64K cash saving is retained); if the second engineer is hired because of self-hosting, their cost must be charged against the $64K and the threshold rises accordingly.'
evidence: The mini-case's own table prices 0.5 FTE at $26K/mo; a second engineer at the same rate is $52K/mo, i.e. 81% of the $64K/month saving the branch is supposed to unlock.

quoted_clause: same per-request price, a different duty cycle
observed: The mini-case inherits the canonical's blended $0.0208/request, but the canonical workload and a RAG assistant have different input/output mixes, and the chapter's own note defines the API line as input×$/1M + output×$/1M-out — linear in volume only at a fixed mix. The entire $64K gap and the 1.9M break-even scale linearly with this price, and the mini-case gives no sensitivity.
correction: State the canonical input/output mix and add a one-line sensitivity of the saving and break-even to the per-request price (e.g., 'at $0.015/request the saving falls to ~$35K/mo and the break-even rises to ~2.7M').
evidence: At $0.015/request: API $75K, saving $35K, break-even 2.67M. At $0.030/request: API $150K, saving $110K, break-even 1.33M. The canonical's own price band ($15–25/1K) moves the saving from $35K to $85K.

quoted_clause: self-host wins only once volume passes the ~7.5M break-even — lower if the staff/ops term is sunk — with sustained near-peak utilization and a benchmark confirming the SLO
observed: At the break-even volume the fleet is nowhere near peak: 7.49M req/mo ÷ 624,000 active s = 12.0 rps against a 40 rps peak, i.e. 30% of peak. The canonical workload's own shape is 10 rps average = 25% of peak. The stated condition 'sustained near-peak utilization' is therefore not met by the workload the chapter analyses and cannot be met at the volume where the crossover occurs.
correction: Replace with the computed condition: 'with the fleet running at ~12 rps of its 40 rps peak (30%) at the crossover — i.e. the fixed-cost advantage is won with substantial idle capacity, which is why this is a frozen-fleet crossover, not a scalable one'.

page_hint: Ch 16 — 'Treat both provisioning policies explicitly' paragraph; provisioning-policy table, last column.

quoted_clause: Utilization = served ÷ provisioned.
observed: Section 4 defines 'Effective utilization' as 'actual goodput ÷ theoretical capacity'. Note 16.1-1 then defines 'Utilization = served ÷ provisioned', which is raw utilization, not effective utilization. If 'served' includes non-SLO-meeting requests, the two definitions conflict and the cost-per-useful-request metric loses its denominator discipline.
correction: Write 'Raw utilization = served ÷ provisioned; effective utilization = SLO-meeting goodput ÷ theoretical capacity.' Use the effective definition wherever cost per useful request is at issue.
evidence: Metric 2: 'Effective utilization — actual goodput ÷ theoretical capacity'. Note 16.1-1: 'Utilization = served ÷ provisioned.' The terms 'served' and 'goodput' are not interchangeable in this chapter's own vocabulary.

quoted_clause: volume sits above the ~7.5M API break-even

The 'When each wins' paragraph nevertheless uses 'the ~7.5M API break-even' as if it were a single threshold. The 7.5M figure is only the midpoint at the canonical $20.8/1K API price; at $15/1K the crossover is ~10.4M and at $25/1K it is ~6.2M.

quoted_clause: W = 8.6 s — the **assumed mean KV-residency time** E[W_KV-resident] (Ch 17's conditional scenario proxy: 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode of GPU execution, with KV assumed held only during execution; the distinct execution estimate 8.58 s is exposed and labeled, never silently substituted

Calling it 'distinct' and 'never silently substituted' tells the reader two different numbers are in play when only one is, and invites a hunt for a difference that does not exist.

Delete 'the distinct execution estimate 8.58 s is exposed and labeled, never silently substituted'.

page_hint: Ch 16 — 'Parametric multi-region worksheet' table, rows 2, 3 and 8.
quoted_clause: | 2 | Failover load | the surviving region must carry 100% of λ_peak = 40 rps | NOT SIZED | … | 3 | Warmed capacity per region | N_region = ⌈λ_region·W_KV/(C·u·ρ)⌉ + N_spare (Table 17-1 formula, applied per region) | NOT SIZED (depends on rows 1–2) | … | 8 | Incremental cost | extra regions + replication + routing/egress — on the order of ≥2× the single-region fleet on the capacity-duplication term alone (above) | NOT PRICED |

As written, a reader who fills row 3 with λ_region = α·40 sizes each region for its share and obtains a fleet smaller than one region sized for peak — contradicting rows 2 and 8.

evidence: With α = 0.5, row 3 gives two regions each sized for 20 rps; the surviving region then admits only ~20 rps against the 40 rps required by row 2. Sizing each region for 40 rps gives 2 × 21 = 42 hosts, which is exactly where '≥2×' comes from.

quoted_clause: The 20 ms used below is the canonical service retrieval round trip — the observed per-request duration of the retrieval service
observed: The decomposition t_net ≈ t_prop/RTT + t_protocol-fixed + D/B_effective + t_queue omits server-side retrieval processing time, even though the 20 ms is described as the observed per-request duration of the retrieval service. If the 20 ms includes vector search, ranking, or other server compute, then t_transfer = t_net − t_prop − t_protocol − t_queue is too large, and D/t_transfer underestimates the instantaneous link rate.
correction: Either define the 20 ms explicitly as a network-only retrieval RTT and remove 'observed per-request duration of the retrieval service,' or add t_service to the decomposition: t_net ≈ t_prop + t_protocol + t_service + D/B_effective + t_queue. Then use t_transfer = D/B_effective for the link check and φ·λ·t_transfer for concurrent network transfers.
evidence: The equation closes only if 20 ms is a network-only round trip. The prose says it is an observed service duration. Those are different populations. The later Little's Law expression φ·λ·t_net also counts service time as if it were network residency, which overstates concurrent network transfers.

quoted_clause: The real headroom is smaller than ~93%.
observed: ~93% is the utilization ratio (demand ÷ ceiling), not the headroom. The headroom under case (i) is ~7%. Under cases (ii) and (iii), demand exceeds the ceiling, so the headroom is negative. The sentence as written is dimensionally/conceptually wrong and understates the problem.
correction: Replace with: 'Under case (i) the available headroom is only ~7%; under cases (ii) and (iii) the prefill leg alone exceeds the idealized ceiling, so the headroom is negative. The real headroom is therefore smaller than the ~7% implied by case (i), and may be negative.'
evidence: Case (i): 18,400/19,780 = 93.0%, so headroom = 7.0%. Case (ii): 109%, headroom = −9%. Case (iii): 101%, headroom = −1%. Saying 'headroom is smaller than ~93%' is not a meaningful bound.
